correctness.rationale: The symmetric two-set-intersection polarity gives F^3=F. Every nonempty image contains a two-set vertex cover; the explicit a,b-spoke membership test exhausts the image shapes and pairs them into all claimed fixed points/two-cycles. Counting inverse fibers gives g_n, h_n and e_n; disjoint basins yield B_n. A union bound proves the n=6 majority cutoff and a pairwise Bonferroni estimate gives the asymptotic. Two separately implemented executable enumerators reproduced all basins at n=5,6 and n=5,6,7 (respectively), covering 2,097,152 labelled states in the largest check. Limits: finite checking alone does not prove all n; that rests on the symbolic cover case analysis.

originality.rationale: The full claim concerns the exact labelled attractor types and six individual basin populations of OPEN-neighborhood NOR on KG(n,2), plus its sharp dominant-basin threshold and asymptotic. The 2015 survey establishes general minterm/maxterm background but not this Kneser census. The examined 2017 and 2020 primary texts use each vertex itself in every local update, unlike the present excluded-self rule; their general period restrictions and periodic-point counting therefore do not imply the statement. Separately, historical formulas for two-set intersecting families do not automatically count exact inverse-NOR fibers. Direct claim comparisons identified no covering result. The original 2012 primary text was not accessible in full, so the conclusion is conditional on that historical-overlap limitation.
residual_risks: Original 2012 article full text not inspected; a previously overlooked equivalent result or special-case table cannot be excluded.

Search-result absence is not proof of novelty; independent expert literature review has not been performed.

value.rationale: The Kneser disjointness graph on two-sets is a canonical infinite structured graph family. Exact attractor counts plus all individual inverse-fiber basin populations are natural dynamical invariants, not arbitrary selected parameters. The complete census yields an unanticipated coexistence of fixed stars/triangles and five types of two-cycles, a sharp n=6 dominance transition and an exponentially small-in-n^2 exceptional probability. The motivation and use of the precise invariants are to distinguish recurrent complexity from basin concentration, without asserting a downstream theorem.
